summary: Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and Oxford. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the London School of Economics, Oxford, and Durham University, where he became Professor of Anthropology.

Michael Comans works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University. He was a faculty member at the University of Sydney (~1989–2005) and served at Sri Venkateswara Temple.
Michael J. Conway specializes in Buddhist studies. He has served as Lecturer of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a faculty member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford (~1963–1967) and under Gudo Wafu Nishijima (~1977–2007). He founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Friedrich specializes in Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich, where he was a Wissenschaftlicher Assistent (1983–1986), and served as Professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.
Michael G. Morony is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a BA at UC Berkeley and an MA at UCLA, where he became a professor in 1974.

Michael Hahn specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He held posts at the University of Bonn and Marburg, where he held the Lehrstuhl für Indologie und Tibetologie (1988–2007).
Michael Harack specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He completed a Master of Arts degree at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at SOAS and the University of London. At SOAS, he served as British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow, South Asia Department Head (1995–1999), and Associate Dean (2002–2010); he also chaired the Britain-Nepal Academic Council.

Michael I. Como works in religious studies, Japanology, and Sinology, having studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. He is the Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University (attested 2009, 2026).

Michael J. Sweet was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He served as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry at Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1996, 2006).
Michael J. Tetreault specializes in religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).
Michael J. Walsh works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, completing his doctorate under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Jochem Schindler and Heiner Eichner, and at the University of Zurich. He held an assistantship at Zurich (1995) and the Indo-European linguistics chair at Münster (2002).

Michael Jansen was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Bonn and RWTH Aachen. He served as Dean of Architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999), Founding Rector of the German University of Technology in Oman (2007–2008), and President of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael Jerryson specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Wisconsin-Madison and completed a PhD under Mark Juergensmeyer at UC Santa Barbara. He held posts at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Cambridge (1969–1972) and SOAS University of London (1987–1990).

Michael L. Walter was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He held positions at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1982, 2020) and the Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000).
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1963–1967) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1980–1988).
